item.title: GRhya first
item.description:
Source: TW

Yajñas are classified into 2 categories- śrauta with 3 fires: gārhapatya, āhavanīya and dakshińa and smārta with single aupāsanāgni. If you look at vedic literature, it’s almost entirely devoted to śrauta (it’s śruti afterall). Gŕhya rituals almost appears as an afterthought.

However, commonsense dictates that a single fire ritual had to have been a precursor. This is exactly what we find in tradition too.

gandharvebhyo varaṃ labdhvā
tretāgniṃ samakalpayat|
eko agniḥ pūrvamāsīd
ailas tretām akalpayat||
(Hari vaṃśa 1.126.47)

item.title: KastUri on fiden's gRhya
item.description:
Intro

Thesis by Fiden called “The Codification and Mobilization of Domestic Religion from the R ̥gveda to the Gr ̥hyasūtras”.

It has lot of useful info and inferences that tally with my own independent study. The final conclusion it was building towards look like Whistler’s mother painting from the movie Bean.

Evolution

Evolution of gṛhya rituals is a topic of great interest to me. The subject material is vast as it stands today with numerous geographical variations. Applying evolutionary principles based on current surviving materials to infer precursors, relationship between shrauta and gṛhya, mutual interactions between various schools, and the position of atharvāngirasa in all these are great topics to investigate. Each one of these would take a lifetime.

item.title: PAkayajna classes
item.description:
Source: TW

By the time of smṛti, nibandha, dharma digests period, the notion of 7 pākayajñas, 7 haviryajñas and 7 somayajñas is well established. Restricting to pākayajñas, we can ask what were those 7 and whether they were always 7.

Applying evolutionary principles, we can actually tease out the temporal layers.

3 pākayajñas

I posit that āśvalāyana is the earliest layer with 3 types of pākayajñas - huta, prahuta and brahmaṇi huta. This is despite śānkhāyana claiming the total of pāka, havis and soma are 21. But it doesn’t evenly divide them into 7 of each types.

item.title: SAma-gRhya
item.description:
Source: TW

Intro

A short thread on homa format of sāmavedins:

I should revisit this sometime- and conclude my notes on gŕhya fire rituals. Since waves of rāmeśvaram calming down is more likely, here’s a note on homa of sāmavedins- especially gobhila tradition. bit.ly/3lD6F2n

Gŕhya rituals require a single fire- typically aupāsana fire as opposed to shrauta requiring 3 fires- gārhapatya, āvahanīya and dakshina.

Prototype

If you examine the homa procedure of different vedas and even tantric agnimukham it should be obvious they all emerged from single prototype.
